title.narrative: Provision of emergency primary health care services to drought affected population in Jowhar district middle shabelle region

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtAccording to the 2023 HRP, less than one third of the people in drought-affected areas are estimated to have access to essential health care. Reported cholera cases continue to rise compared to recent years, while measles cases have spiked, particularly among children. The FSNAU post Deyr assessment results shows that global acute malnutrition has remained critical (15.4% lt/spangtltspan style="color: black font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gt lt/spangtltspan style="color: black font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtin 2022 Deyr season, from 15.9% in 2022 Gu). According to the 2023 HNO, about 1.8 million children under five are likely to face acute malnutrition through mid-2023 including over 513,000 who are expected to be severely malnourished. Malnutrition rates are at unacceptable high levels particularly in Jowhar districtlt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="color: black font-family: Calibri, sans-serif"gtThe project aims to provide life-saving emergency primary health care to 15,000(2,500 men, 5,500 women, 3,500 girls and 3,500 girls) drought displaced pastoral hard to reach areas and host communities in Jowhar y district through two static and four mobile clinics through provision of maternal and neonatal and child Health Care as well as immunization to the target lt5 children boys, girls including disables. The primary health care center will provide outpatient consultations to both men, women, boys, girls including disable group, ante-natal and post-natal care, skilled delivery birth attendants and services, immunization, treatment of common childhood diseases, health education through social mobilization with integration of mental health and psychosocial support services, gender based violence’s including clinical rape management. Capacity building of local health staffs will be strengthened in order to provide quality health care to the community. The Maternal Child Health will be operational for all days due to the facility delivery needs and emergency referral. Building the capacity of health workers through training on Basic Emergency Obstetric Care (BEmOC) will be done to equip health workers with the required skills to deliver quality health care services to the affected population.SRC through this project will provide life-saving medical consultations and medical drugs supply to the health facility, establish mental health and GBV referral mechanisms between SRC facilities and secondary healthcare providers in Jowhar y district Middle shabelle region, improve the coverage of measles vaccinations and support safe motherhood and reproductive health while also ensuring readiness to prevent and respond to outbreaks of AWD/Cholera and promote health update while ensuring early warning and surveillance information sharing to the health cluster. Integration of Mental Health/Psycho-social Support (PFA) services, community engagement, and health education to community members to enhance identification and referral of persons of concern in need of MHPSS while also conducting a focused MHPSS intervention through trained social workers. Conduct psycho-education sessions for persons in need, including raising awareness on key protection risks faced by PSNs i.e discrimination, stigma targeting people in Jowhar district. The MHSS team will consist of, midwife (ANC), register /auxiliary nurse) and counsellor. We shall commit to provide regular updates and reports to the SHF on any project developments, progress and issues and maintain the coordination with all concerned. A Conflict-Sensitive Approach will be implemented throughout the project cycle, guided by our Conflict-Sensitive Field Manual, tools, security, risk and emergency procedures. Resilience operations are assured through our risk reporting protocols and minimum operating security standards (to staff, beneficiaries, infrastructure, and resources). Services provided by the mobile clinics will be monitored through a file tracking system that will ensure accurate input of data for every registered patientlt/spangtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-family: Calibri, sans-serif color: black"gt
